name: Plane (open-source)
team_execution_depth: Plane offers a credible team-execution layer modelled directly on Linear, with rich work items (rich text, attachments, comments, sub-issues, custom states), Cycles (sprints with burndown), Modules (thematic groupings), Epics, and Pages. The 2025 product reorganised Cycles, Modules, Epics, and Pages as horizontal tabs inside each project, putting the daily execution surface front-and-centre rather than burying it in a sidebar. Boards support Kanban/List/Calendar with grouping and sorting by label/state, and a Power K 2.0 command palette landed October 2025. The system feels purpose-built for an engineering squad of 5-30 people; story points, estimates, sub-issues, labels, and custom states are all first-class. Where it lags Linear is in opinionated workflow defaults — Plane gives flexibility but does less of the 'right thing' automatically — and dedicated scrum master views (capacity planning, ceremony templates) are thinner than Jira's.
keyboard_command_ux: Power K (Cmd+K) command palette is the headline keyboard surface, refreshed as Power K 2.0 in October 2025 with faster fuzzy search across work items, cycles, modules, projects, docs and analytics, plus the ability to create new items directly from the palette. A full shortcut sheet (Cmd+/) covers status changes, navigation, cycle/module/page actions, and work-item assignment. Plane explicitly positions itself as keyboard-first and the gap to Linear's sub-100ms feel has narrowed, though community comparisons still rate Linear's overall snap as marginally tighter. [uncertain] Precise P50/P95 latency benchmarks against Linear are not published.
ui_responsiveness: Plane is a React + Django stack served over standard HTTP — not a local-first sync engine like Linear's. Public comparisons describe Plane as capturing roughly 80 percent of Linear's speed and elegance, with most interactions feeling fast but occasional server round-trips on filter/board changes. Self-hosted deployments depend on the host's infra: a well-provisioned cluster feels snappy; an under-provisioned VPS does not. [uncertain] No published P50/P95 numbers from Plane or independent benchmarks.
real_time_collaboration: Threaded replies on work-item comments shipped December 2025, alongside Intake forms and revised workspace navigation. @mentions, activity logs, and notifications exist; Pages support real-time co-editing. Live presence indicators on boards and cards are present but less prominent than Linear's. Slack integration lets conversations be promoted to Plane work items. The collaboration layer is competent but not the headline experience — Plane still expects teams to use Slack/Teams for real-time chat rather than positioning itself as a chat-replacement like Height did.
mobile_experience: Native iOS and Android apps (open-source repo `makeplane/plane-mobile`) cover assigns/mentions/comments alerts, project overview, view/edit/add issues, and Cycle/Module progress tracking with Kanban/List/Calendar layouts. The same app works for cloud and self-hosted logins. Sprint board parity with desktop is reasonable for status updates and quick edits, though deeper planning workflows still want the desktop. [uncertain] Offline capability for the mobile app is not clearly documented — Plane references signed offline bundles for the self-hosted server, but mobile-side offline editing is not a stated feature.
in_tool_documentation: Pages are first-class — nested pages, doc imports, embeds, and inline references mean acceptance criteria, decision logs, and meeting notes can live next to the work items. The September 2025 release added doc imports and nested pages explicitly to make Plane a 'projects and docs in one workspace' tool, directly attacking the Jira-plus-Confluence and Notion-plus-Jira combos.
developer_experience: Strong for an OSS tool. The Plane MCP server (official, open-source) exposes six tools out of the box (create_cycle, list_issues, update_issue, etc.) and supports stdio, SSE, and streamable HTTP transports, with documented Claude Code integration. A VS Code MCP integration lets developers manage work items inside the editor. CLI is implicit via API/MCP rather than a dedicated binary. Branch/PR/commit visibility on cards is provided through the GitHub integration. Code-review status as a board column is achievable through state customisation but not preset. [uncertain] A native JetBrains plugin does not appear to exist.
vcs_integration_depth: Two-way GitHub sync: issues created in GitHub flow into Plane and back, with comments and updates synced; Plane work items can be linked to PRs and commits for traceability. GitHub Enterprise integration shipped October 2025. GitLab integration syncs issues, merge requests, and commits. Sentry integration syncs issues. Auto-state transitions on PR open/merge are achievable but require workflow configuration; branch-naming-convention enforcement is not a documented out-of-the-box feature. The depth is closer to Linear's GitHub integration than to Jira's mature 10-year-old app, but it is materially deeper than ServiceNow EAP's.
ai_agentic_maturity: Notably mature for an open-source tool. Plane AI 'reads across every project, cycle, doc, and thread' in the workspace; built-in agents triage incoming requests, assign owners, track blockers, and ship updates. Plane ships an Agent Development Kit and an open-source MCP server, and the Marketplace (launched 2025) hosts integrations, importers, and third-party agents. Documented Claude Code integration via MCP is a first-class story. This is materially ahead of Jira-equivalent OSS competitors and competitive with Linear's MCP server, though it sits behind Linear's published '75 percent of enterprise workspaces using agents' adoption data. [uncertain] Plane's own enterprise adoption metrics for agents are not public.
time_to_value: Cloud free tier is genuinely free-forever for up to 12 users with core Cycles/Modules/Pages; sign-up to first sprint board is minutes, not days. Self-hosted deployment via Docker Compose or Helm with sub-2GB images is among the lightest in the category. The product is intentionally less configuration-heavy than Jira — projects, cycles, and modules are the primary scaffold, and templates exist for common team shapes. Steeper than Linear (which is more opinionated) but materially faster to first value than Jira or ServiceNow EAP.
migration_story: Jira Cloud importer migrates projects, issues, and users with field mapping and history. Asana, ClickUp, and CSV importers are documented. GitHub issue importer is available. This is one of Plane's marketed differentiators — explicit positioning as the destination for 'I am leaving Jira/Asana/ClickUp' migrations. [uncertain] Field-mapping coverage for complex Jira workflows (custom screens, automation rules, advanced fields) and post-migration data continuity guarantees are not detailed in public docs.
deprecation_transition_risk: Low. Plane is an actively developed OSS project (~31K GitHub stars, 100+ contributors, 500K+ Docker pulls), aggressive 2025 release cadence (monthly changelogs), and a stated open-core sustainability model. AGPL v3.0 license on the Community Edition. Risks: company-funded OSS vendor change (license shift) is a theoretical concern as with any open-core company; self-hosted Free is capped at 12 users which can force a Pro upgrade as teams grow.
safe_framework_alignment: Weak. Plane is a team-level tool by design — Cycles, Modules, Epics, and Initiatives provide a small portfolio hierarchy, but PI Planning UX, ART boards, Program Increment burndown, Capability/Feature/Story SAFe taxonomy, cross-ART dependency mapping, WSJF prioritisation, and inspect-and-adapt rituals are not first-class. It can be bent into a flat 'project = ART' shape but the ceremonial scaffolding that SAFe customers expect (and that ServiceNow EAP provides) is absent.
reporting_metrics: Cycles produce burndown charts. Analytics surface velocity and basic flow metrics. Custom dashboards in Business and above. Reports are functional rather than category-leading — there is no equivalent to Planview's flow-metrics-first treatment, and CFD/throughput/lead-time as configurable first-class charts are weaker than dedicated flow tools. Acceptable for a team layer, undersized for portfolio reporting.
customer_signal_ingestion: Intake (renamed to custom Intake forms in December 2025) accepts external requests into a triage queue; Slack-to-work-item supports inbound signal capture. There is no native NPS, feature-vote, or support-ticket ingestion comparable to Productboard.
integration_ecosystem: GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, Slack, Sentry, VS Code MCP, Jira/Asana/ClickUp/CSV importers, and an open Marketplace launched 2025 for community integrations and agents. Figma is not listed as a native integration as of the latest changelogs. The marketplace is young (months old, not years) and small relative to Jira's 5,000+-app ecosystem.
community_vitality: Healthy for its age. ~31K GitHub stars (#1 in the open-source PM category by stars), 100+ contributors, 500K+ Docker pulls. Active GitHub Discussions, monthly changelog cadence, Launch Week Fall 2025. Discord and Reddit presence exists but is modest compared to Linear/Notion. Marketplace and third-party content libraries are nascent.
self_hosting_data_residency: This is Plane's flagship differentiator. Three self-hosted editions: open-source Community (AGPL v3.0), Commercial, and Airgapped. Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, six documented deployment methods, sub-2GB image. Explicitly markets GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2 compliance posture via customer control of data. The Airgapped Edition with signed offline bundles and zero external calls is targeted at defence, government, and regulated finance — directly the EU/government niche the brief calls out.
customization: Custom work-item types, custom fields, custom states, custom views, project templates (Business+), workflow rules and approvals (Business+). Workflow builder is competent but less deep than Jira's, and admins cannot reshape screens to the same degree. Reasonable middle ground between Linear's opinionated rigidity and Jira's configuration sprawl.
pricing_commercial_model: Free Community (self-hosted, AGPL, no user cap on self-host) and Free Cloud (up to 12 users). Pro $6/seat/month (Wiki, time tracking, custom work-item types, Epics, Initiatives, SAML SSO). Business $13/seat/month annual (workflows, approvals, intake, RBAC, nested pages, project templates, advanced dashboards, 2x AI credits). Enterprise Grid for multi-workspace, LDAP, SCIM, airgapped, audit logs. 5 free Guest slots per paid seat. Same price for cloud or self-hosted. Materially cheaper than Jira Premium ($16.50) and Notion Business ($20-24), well below ServiceNow EAP's per-portfolio commercial model.
total_cost_of_ownership: Low per-seat list price ($6-13). Self-hosted carries the usual ops overhead: containers, Postgres, object storage, upgrades, backups. Operational FTE cost is real but small for a competent platform team. No mandatory implementation consulting. The cost story is the inverse of ServiceNow EAP — cheap to license, you pay in self-hosted ops effort if you choose that path. [uncertain] Published 3-year TCO benchmarks against Jira or ServiceNow are not available.
market_perception: Niche-darling reputation. Strong sentiment among self-hosting, EU-government, and data-sovereignty buyers; quoted as 'everything a self-hosted PM tool should be in 2025'. Not yet positioned in Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Agile Planning Tools. G2/Capterra review volume is small compared to Jira or Notion. Developer Reddit/HN sentiment is broadly positive but cautious — a frequent 'we replaced Jira with Plane' anecdote pattern. [uncertain] Specific Gartner Peer Insights and aggregated G2 score with review count not surfaced.
gaps_vs_market_leader: Versus Jira: no SAFe PI Planning, no ART-level taxonomy, marketplace 5000x smaller, no formal Gartner positioning, weaker enterprise admin governance, no native time-tracking ecosystem of third-party apps. Versus Linear: not local-first, not as polished or as fast in P50 perceived latency, fewer opinionated defaults, weaker mobile parity for power workflows, smaller user community. Versus ServiceNow EAP: no portfolio/strategy layer, no native ITSM/ITIL linkage, no Now Platform data-model integration. Severities: SAFe absence and portfolio layer are showstoppers for SAFe-mandated enterprises; the rest are frictions.
